# Independent audit: exact sector-feasibility PSD criterion

Source: `candidate 2e26c63010f03ffc`, Sections 1–7. Result: **PASS**, including singular matrices, zero-excess sectors, and exact finite reconstruction.

The geometric input is precisely the proved reciprocal feasibility system. The harmonic edge condition is algebraically equivalent after r_i=a_i/(D_i u_i), s_i=a_i/(D_i v_i). Positive h_i forces finite charges strictly greater than h_i. The relaxed edge region is closed and convex; scaling a feasible positive pair by h_i/H_i lowers both node charges and restores its exact harmonic value. A zero edge can be set to zero without affecting feasibility, corresponding exactly to t_i=1 and u_i=v_i=1/2.

The budget upper set is nonempty and convex. Its closedness proof is valid: a convergent budget sequence bounds every nonnegative individual charge by one of its finite node budgets, so a common subsequence of all finitely many charges converges inside the closed edge regions. The nearest-point separation argument yields a nonnegative separating vector from upward closure, with a strict squared-distance gap. No hidden Slater assumption, dual attainment, or compactness of the unbounded edge sets is used.

The dual cost has the correct index orientation, theta_(i+1) r_i+theta_i s_i. Weighted arithmetic-geometric mean gives exactly h_i(sqrt(theta_i)+sqrt(theta_(i+1)))^2. When a coefficient is zero this is an infimum attained only as a charged variable approaches h_i and its free partner diverges; the proof explicitly uses an infimum and handles this correctly. The separated finite infimum is legitimate for every nonnegative theta.

The matrix is a symmetric Z-matrix. Replacing any vector by its coordinatewise absolute value lowers or preserves its quadratic form. Therefore the derived copositivity condition is equivalent to positive semidefiniteness. The quadratic-form definition avoids cyclic-entry ambiguities for small m.

Section 7 also supplies a complete independent constructive proof. Each block's Rayleigh minimum exists on its unit sphere. Absolute values preserve minimality because the off-diagonal entries are nonpositive. A nonnegative least eigenvector on a positive-edge connected component is strictly positive: any zero coordinate forces every positive-edge neighbor to vanish, and then the entire connected component. Singleton components are treated separately. PSD supplies a positive vector w with Lw>=0 even if the least eigenvalue is zero.

The stated formulas for r_i,s_i have harmonic value h_i and turn Lw>=0 into the exact node budgets. The recovered u_i,v_i are positive, sum to t_i, and are finite, so the already proved sector construction yields an actual polygon. The converse Gram identity expands to diagonal b_i-h_(i-1)-h_i and off-diagonal -h_i exactly: s_i^2/(r_i+s_i)=s_i-h_i and r_i^2/(r_i+s_i)=r_i-h_i. Zero edges contribute no term. Thus the direct proof includes the degeneracies without a spectral-gap limit.

The result is an exact ordinary planar ray/sector realization criterion. It does not independently establish the desired section-weight implication or preserve inter-fiber compatibility.
